claims.text: A quinary, equiatomic or near-equiatomic Al-Cr-Co-Fe-Ni alloy is a candidate system for the proposed method.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid states near the alloy's melting temperature.
The intervention is an augmented EAM or other extended many-body potential containing explicit configuration-dependent corrections.
The configuration-dependent corrections will be calibrated against ab initio liquid configurations.
The corrected potential will represent the diversity of local atomic environments in the liquid better than conventional EAM references.
The corrected potential will substantially improve reference-target phase-space overlap relative to TOR-TILD's conventional EAM references.
TOR-TILD's conventional EAM references fail to capture the full configurational diversity of the ab initio liquid.
More accurate representation of liquid structural fluctuations will produce a smoother thermodynamic-integration path with fewer reference-target mismatches.
The thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will be reduced by approximately 40% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
The method is applicable to high-entropy alloys containing at least five near-equiatomic elements.
The applicable temperature range is approximately 0.8 to 1.0 times the melting temperature.
Performance for non-equiatomic alloys or temperatures far from melting is uncertain.
The proposed potential and baseline EAM reference will be compared through thermodynamic-integration calculations on the same high-entropy alloy over 0.8 Tm to Tm.
The comparison will measure integration-path mismatch, free-energy convergence, and reference-target phase-space overlap.
Absolute free-energy differences will be benchmarked against ab initio free-energy calculations.
The hypothesis is falsified if the new potential produces less than a 10% reduction in path mismatch or fails to improve phase-space overlap relative to the EAM reference.
